fix(claude-code): preserve existing settings.json configuration on reconfigure (#3)

Previously, clicking Configure/Reconfigure would overwrite the entire
settings.json with only `env` and `model` keys, losing user's custom
configuration like permissions, hooks, mcpServers, statusLine, and plugins.

Now implements smart merge behavior:
- Reads existing settings.json before writing
- Merges env object: preserves user's keys (MCP_API_KEY, PAI_DIR, etc.),
  updates only Quotio-managed ANTHROPIC_* keys
- Preserves ALL other top-level configuration
- Timestamped backups still created on each reconfigure (never overwritten)

This mirrors the existing merge pattern used in generateOpenCodeConfig.

Validation, YAML emission, the Fetch Models request and the pre-save
connection test each saw a different form of the same header list, so a
name entered as " X-Tenant-ID " passed validation and produced correct
YAML while CFNetwork serialized the request line as a continuation of
Host.

Introduce a single canonical representation and route every consumer
through it:

  unnamed entries. The editor persists this form.
- CustomProvider.effectiveHeaders is the one accessor used by YAML
  emission and both URLRequest paths; it also filters entries that
  validation would reject so providers stored before this change cannot
  produce a corrupt request or an invalid config.

  shared by Fetch Models and the connection test.
- Fetch Models now validates the canonical set before applying it.

Also reject header values that are not RFC 7230 field-value safe (CR/LF,
other control characters, non-ASCII), which closes header injection via
a value, and replace the partial YAML escaper with the complete
double-quoted escape set so emission round-trips losslessly.

feat: add optional YubiKey secret vault (#490)

* feat: add optional YubiKey secret vault

* fix(yubikey): non-destructive headless provisioning and honest vault status

Addresses the review on #490.

Provisioning no longer opens a Terminal window. The sheet collects the PIV
PIN once and runs ykman headlessly, feeding credentials over stdin rather
than argv, which any same-uid process can read via ps. Preflight parses
`ykman piv info` and refuses to call slot 9d empty unless firmware >= 5.3
can prove it; below that, and when no PIV version is reported, the slot is
`.unknown` and treated as destructive. The number of credential lines is
derived from whether the management key is already PIN-protected, because
ykman only prompts for it when it is not -- feeding a stray line would
shift the PIN onto the wrong prompt and burn a PIN attempt.

Settings now reports what the vault is actually doing: active with the key
name, fingerprint and protected-secret count; configured-but-disconnected;
or not configured. Previously nothing distinguished a successful setup from
an untouched one.

Fix identity discovery, which never matched. availableIdentities() compared
kSecAttrTokenID against the driver bundle id "com.apple.CryptoTokenKit.
pivtoken", but macOS reports the token *instance* -- the driver id with the
card UUID appended, e.g. "com.apple.pivtoken:48B9336C...". The equality could
not hold, so every PIV identity was filtered out and setup always ended on
"not configured".

Make the post-setup message match reality. It previously read "choose the key
below" in three cases where nothing was below: no identity published, already
configured, or the change blocked by existing secrets. Each now has its own
message, and the section renders one coherent story per state instead of
repeating the same prompt three ways.

Localize the whole flow: 45 keys across en, fr, vi and zh-Hans. Untranslated
keys render as raw key strings, so a French user previously saw a header
reading "settings.yubikey.title". Counts use %lld -- String(format:) bridges
Int as 64-bit, so %d would read the wrong half.

Tests cover parsePreflight against fixtures rendered through ykman's own
pretty-printer, and the token-id match against the instance id observed on
a YubiKey 5C NFC (5.4.3).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(yubikey): stop a failed vault read from rolling a credential back

A caller that cannot read a secret sees only nil, and cannot tell "never
stored" from "hardware key unavailable". CLIProxyManager.init does exactly
that: read, and on nil mint a fresh UUID and save it. With the vault on and
the key unplugged -- or the PIN prompt dismissed, which --pin-policy always
raises on every read -- that permanently overwrote the envelope holding the
real management key.

Guard the single choke point every such path funnels through. saveData now
refuses to overwrite an envelope it could not read; .absent stays writable
so first-time storage and legacy migration still work, and costs only a
file-existence check, so no write pays for a decrypt it does not need.

readData's vault branch now calls shouldMigrateLegacy instead of restating
the rule inline. The function had no production caller, so its test only
proved it agreed with itself.

Also skip testMonitorCredentialVaultAddsRotatesAndDeletesAPIKeys when the
vault is enabled. The test host shares the app's defaults, so on a machine
with a configured key it drove the real hardware: six PIN prompts, 90
seconds, and a failure.

fix: keep Claude Code credentials read-only (#526)

Quotio is a usage monitor and should not interfere with the CLI it observes.
Reading is not the boundary — refreshing is, because a refresh spends a token
the Claude Code CLI also holds.

The CLI treats that token as a serialized, single-use resource: it guards
refresh with a cross-process lock, detects sibling races, and marks a refresh
token it did not spend itself as dead on `invalid_grant`. An unsynchronized
refresh from Quotio can therefore push the CLI into that dead-token state and
sign the user out of Claude Code.

Three paths were doing exactly that:

- `CompositeClaudeQuotaCredentialLoader` refreshed the `Claude Code-credentials`
  keychain item and wrote the result back via compare-and-swap.
- `LocalClaudeQuotaCredentialLoader` refreshed and rewrote
  `~/.claude/.credentials.json` in place.
- `ClaudeDesktopCredentialReader`'s credential went through the same refresh
  branch as the rest.

All three now read only. An expired access token yields no fresh quota until
the CLI renews it itself, which is the correct outcome for an observer. A
read-only credential that fails authentication falls back to cached data rather
than reporting `isForbidden`, which would ask the user to sign in to Quotio for
a credential Quotio does not manage.

Ownership is carried on the credential rather than implied by the call site.
`ClaudeQuotaCredential.allowsRefresh` is the single gate the fetcher and both
loaders consult, and `ClaudeCredentialOwnership` decides it for auth files by
the directory they live in — honouring `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` the way the CLI does.

Symlinked auth files are never refreshed: a `claude-*.json` entry under
`~/.cli-proxy-api` pointing at `~/.claude/.credentials.json` would otherwise be
treated as ours and spend the CLI's token through the link. AGENTS.md requires
auth files never be followed through a symlink destination, so this fails closed.

Files under `~/.cli-proxy-api/` that Quotio and the bundled proxy own, and
accounts in Quotio's own vault, still refresh as before.

feat: improve Card and Ring quota layouts (#527)

Makes the reset countdown the legible, equal-weight companion to the bar or
ring in both styles, and gives the Ring style a real `Grid` so label, ring and
caption share one baseline.

Addresses the four issues raised in review of #449:

1. Window captions come from the metric's own identity, never its display name.
   `Session` is produced by Claude's five-hour window, by Codex's variable
   window of up to 24 hours and by Z.ai alike, so a single "4h window" caption
   would be wrong for most of them. `QuotaMetricWindow` reads the duration from
   the raw identity and only when that identity states one; anything else omits
   the caption rather than guessing. Calendar-variable "monthly" is deliberately
   omitted.

2. Unknown quotas are not rendered as measurements. A percentage outside
   0...100 is the "no data" sentinel; Card and Ring now show an availability
   placeholder, and the menu ring's centre label renders one too instead of
   printing "-1". "off" is not used — nothing here signals an enabled state.
   This builds on `ringPercent` / `RingProgressView.unknownPercent` already on
   `master` rather than introducing a parallel mechanism.

   Standalone metrics are the exception and are handled as one: Amp/OpenRouter
   balances and Grok status set the sentinel deliberately and carry their value
   in `formattedUsage`, so that value is read before the sentinel is consulted.

3. Unlimited metrics with usage are not labelled "unused". Cursor's on-demand
   spend reports 100% remaining because it has no ceiling, while carrying a
   non-zero used count, so "123 used" became "unused". `isUnlimitedUsage`
   carries the distinction and usage is preferred for these; "unused" is
   reserved for a genuinely zero-used window. The Card row no longer suppresses
   usage for metrics without a typed presentation — which is what hid the
   affected metrics in the first place.

4. Rings occupy stable semantic columns. `RingSlotArrangement` pins Session and
   Weekly to fixed positions and leaves a placeholder when one is absent, so an
   account without a Session window no longer slides Weekly into the first
   column. Semantic columns are only reserved for providers that use that
   vocabulary. The dashboard and the menu share this arrangement rather than
   each implementing its own, so the two views cannot disagree about the same
   account.

   Rows wrap at four columns instead of truncating: a provider reporting more
   than four metrics (Kiro appends both a bonus and a base metric per breakdown
   entry) previously lost the extras, which the old `LazyVGrid` had wrapped.
   Dashboard columns are a fixed width, so the separate `Grid` instances line up
   with each other across account cards.

   Each ring carries an accessibility label naming the metric, its value and its
   window, and the menu ring shows the metric name again — without it a row of
   rings gives no way to tell Session from Weekly from Extra.

`isUnlimitedUsage` lives with the other `QuotaMetric` presentation helpers, and
`QuotaMetricWindow` / `RingSlotArrangement` with the shared Presentation
components, so Domain stays free of display rules.

fix(ci): actually run the architecture check (#531)

The architecture check has never run in CI, and has been reporting success.

`report_matches` invoked `rg` inside an `if` condition, so `set -e` could not
fire and any non-zero exit was read as "no matches found". `rg` exits 1 for no
match, but also 127 when it is not installed — and the `macos-15` runner image
does not ship ripgrep. Every `verify` job therefore produced thirteen
`command not found` lines on stderr, matched nothing, printed
"Architecture check passed" and exited 0.

So the boundaries this script defines have been unenforced since it was added:
Domain importing SwiftUI, Presentation reaching for FileManager, a reintroduced
`static let shared` — none of it would have failed a build.

Two changes to the script, both failing closed:

- A preflight `command -v rg` guard exits 2 with an actionable message,
  matching the existing convention for a missing source directory.
- `report_matches` distinguishes rg's exit codes. Only 1 means "ran, found
  nothing"; 0 is a violation, and anything higher now exits 2 naming the check
  that could not run, instead of passing silently.

The guard alone would turn a silent pass into a hard CI failure, so the
workflow installs ripgrep before the check runs.

Current `master` passes all thirteen checks once they actually execute, so
enabling them requires no other source changes.

Verified by running the script with `rg` absent from PATH (exits 2 rather than
printing "passed"), with a stub `rg` that exits 2 (names the check that could
not run), and against a planted `static let shared` in Presentation to confirm
real violations are still caught.
